name: No-Boil Chicken Pasta Casserole with Artichokes and Peas

ingredients.buy: 12 oz (2 1/3 of the 5.2 oz packages), crumbled
1 lb 4 oz drained (about 2 1/3 cans), roughly chopped
2 1/3 tsp finely grated (zest of the same lemons)

writer_notes: DISH SIZE FLAG: transcription specifies a single 9x13 dish, but all ingredients are scaled x2.333 to reach 14 servings. One 9x13 cannot hold this volume, so the prose directs a large roasting pan or two 9x13 dishes. If the engine intends a single dish, servings or scale should be reviewed.

Fractional packages: build calls for 2 1/3 Boursin packages and ~2 1/3 cans of artichokes. Shop Smart tells shoppers to buy 3 of each and expect leftovers. No cost claim made, pure quantity guidance from the buy strings.
No cost_lines were provided in this dispatch, so shop_smart contains zero per-package or per-ounce cost comparisons. Only cost_ps (token) and the dollar-a-month membership line carry money.
All 13 locked ingredients are used by a step and no step uses anything unbought (verified both directions).
Pasta is the real carbohydrate source satisfying the run condition.

prose.intro_html:
Here is a weeknight truth most people never test: you do not have to boil the pasta first. This one is a dump-and-bake, which means the raw penne cooks right in the sauce while it sits in the oven. You blend a creamy base, layer everything cold, cover it, and walk away. No pot of boiling water, no colander, no second pan to wash.

And do not let the cottage cheese scare you off. Blended smooth with a package of Boursin, a little garlic, lemon, and salt, it turns into a silky sauce that bakes down around the pasta and coats every bite. The artichokes and peas keep it from feeling heavy, the lemon keeps it bright, and the chicken breast does the heavy lifting on protein. You are looking at nearly 55 grams of protein a serving for about 603 calories. That is a real dinner, not a sad diet plate.
prose.shop_smart:
The build wants 1 lb 12 oz of dry penne. That is basically two one-pound boxes with a little left in the second, so grab two and keep the rest in the pantry for next time. Cubed chicken breast comes in at 3 1/2 lb, which is one family pack at most stores.

The sauce leans on two dairy items. You need 2 lb 5 oz of cottage cheese, so a standard large tub covers it with a bit to spare. For the Boursin, the build calls for 2 1/3 of the 5.2 oz Garlic and Fine Herbs packages, so buy 3 and you will have a little left over to spread on toast. Same idea on the artichoke hearts: the recipe uses about 2 1/3 cans drained, so pick up 3 cans and drain them well.

Frozen peas are your friend here, no need to buy fresh, and they go in straight from the bag. For the parmesan, buy a wedge and grate it yourself, since the recipe is built on freshly grated and it melts into that golden top far better than the powdery stuff. Two lemons give you both the juice and the zest the sauce needs, so buy them together and zest before you juice.
prose.make_it:
Heat the oven to 400 degrees F. Grease your baking vessel and set it aside. One note that matters at this size: a full 14-serving batch is a lot of casserole, so use a large roasting pan or split it across two 9x13 dishes. Do not try to cram it all into one 9x13, it will overflow and the middle will never cook through.

Make the sauce first. In a blender or food processor, combine the cottage cheese, crumbled Boursin, minced garlic, fresh lemon juice, lemon zest, and sea salt. Blend until completely smooth, then pour in the chicken broth and blend again until it is silky and fully combined. It will look very thin, and that is exactly right. That thin sauce is the water your pasta is going to drink while it bakes.

Now assemble. Spread the dry penne across the bottom of your dish. Scatter the cubed chicken, the peas, and the chopped artichoke hearts over the top. Pour the blended sauce over everything and make sure every bit of pasta is submerged. Any noodle poking out of the liquid will bake up hard, so press them down under the surface.

Cover tightly with foil and bake for 40 minutes. Pull it out, take off the foil, and give it a good stir. The pasta should be just shy of done at this point. Top with the grated parmesan and return it to the oven uncovered for another 5 to 10 minutes, and you can bump the temperature up to get that top golden. If the pasta already feels done when you stir it, just top with parmesan and let it rest.

Let the whole thing rest at least 10 minutes before you touch it. The sauce sets up and stops running as it cools. Then scatter the parsley or basil over the top and you are ready to portion.
prose.portion_html:
This batch fills 14 containers. The honest way to split it evenly is to weigh the pot, not eyeball the scoops. Set your empty casserole vessel on the scale and note the weight, or weigh a clean empty container. Then weigh the finished, rested casserole, subtract the dish, and divide the food weight by 14. That number is your target per container.

Portion by that weight, first pass a little light so you do not run short at the end, then go back and top each one up to even. A casserole like this settles and firms as it cools, so let it rest fully before you divide it or you will chase a moving target. Fourteen containers, each landing near 55 grams of protein, is the goal.
prose.cost_closing_html:
At ${{cost_ps}} a serving, this is what a smart dinner is supposed to cost. Fourteen meals off one oven session, no takeout, no drive-through, no wondering where the money went. You did the work once and you eat all week.

That is the whole Thrifty Crew idea. Real food, real protein, real math, and a membership that runs you a dollar a month. Cook once, count the savings, repeat.

head.description: A no-boil, dump-and-bake chicken pasta casserole with artichokes, peas, and a creamy blended cottage cheese and Boursin sauce. High protein, budget friendly, and scaled to 14 meal-prep servings.
head.keywords: no boil chicken pasta casserole, dump and bake pasta, high protein meal prep, chicken artichoke casserole, cottage cheese pasta sauce, budget meal prep dinner, penne casserole
steps: Preheat the oven to 400 degrees F and grease your baking dish. For a full 14-serving batch, use a large roasting pan or split across two 9x13 dishes.

In a blender or food processor, blend the cottage cheese, crumbled Boursin, minced garlic, fresh lemon juice, lemon zest, and sea salt until smooth, then blend in the chicken broth until silky and thin.
Spread the dry penne in the dish, scatter the cubed chicken, peas, and chopped artichoke hearts over it, then pour the sauce over everything so all the pasta is submerged.
Cover tightly with foil and bake for 40 minutes. Remove the foil, stir, top with grated parmesan, and bake uncovered another 5 to 10 minutes until the top is golden.
Rest at least 10 minutes so the sauce sets, garnish with parsley or basil, then portion into 14 containers.
